chapters.text: Here's a test every bag should pass. One hand holds a coffee. The other has to find your things and shut the bag again, all while you keep walking.
Most bags want both hands, one to hold the bag and one to fight the catch. This one has a clasp that snaps shut with one hand. So watch it do exactly that.
Coffee in your left hand. Right hand on the clasp. One press, and it snaps shut. No fumbling, no second hand, and the coffee never moves.
Now open it again, still one-handed. Your phone, wallet and keys each have their own spot, so there's no digging through the bottom of the bag.
Result: coffee still full, bag still shut, and one hand left over. That's a pass.
The secret is that one-hand clasp. And when your hands get busier, the adjustable strap goes from handbag to crossbody, so the bag stays out of your way.

chapters.text: Say your best friend has a long Saturday coming up. Brunch, a few errands, a walk, then dinner. She asks which bag she should carry.
Tell her to pick one with an adjustable strap. Short, it's a handbag for brunch. Longer, it's a crossbody for the walk.
Because the strap does the work. Nothing else in her day has to change: same bag, same things inside, just worn another way.
And tell her to pick a bag that shuts properly. This one has a clasp that snaps shut with one hand, so a coffee in the other is no problem.
Inside, her phone, wallet and keys each get their own spot, so nothing sinks to the bottom while she's out all day.

chapters.text: Tomorrow is a long day out. Brunch, a few errands, dinner after, and no time to go home in between. So tonight, you pack the bag.
Phone goes in first. Then your wallet, then your keys. Open it up and each one has its own spot, so there's room for everything and nothing piles up at the bottom.
While you're at it, set the strap. It's adjustable, so you choose the length tonight: handbag or crossbody, ready before you leave.
Then the last step. One hand on the clasp, and it snaps shut. That's tomorrow's bag, packed and ready, and it took no time at all.
Morning. You pick it up, it's already packed, and you head out the door. Over the shoulder, and a hand ready for the coffee.
Worn crossbody or carried as a handbag, it sits where you set it, and the day goes on around it.
